### [IgrHighlight](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrHighlight)
Searches the text projected into its default slot and highlights the matches.
It uses the native CSS Custom Highlight API, so it does not change the DOM.

The component supports case-sensitive matching and programmatic navigation between
matches. Navigation scrolls the active match into view. When the content changes,
the component searches it again and keeps the active match where it can.

- **caseSensitive**: `boolean` — Whether the matching distinguishes upper and lower case.
When true, only exact-case occurrences of searchText are highlighted.
- **searchText**: `string` — The string to search and highlight in the DOM content of the component.
A change of this property starts a new search.
An empty string clears all highlights.
- **current**: `any` — The zero-based index of the active match. Returns `0` when there are no matches.
- **size**: `any` — The total number of matches found for the current `searchText`. Returns `0` when there are no matches or `searchText` is empty.
- **next**(options?: HighlightNavigation): void — Moves the active highlight to the next match.
Wraps around to the first match after the last one.
- **previous**(options?: HighlightNavigation): void — Moves the active highlight to the previous match.
Wraps around to the last match when going back from the first one.
- **search**(): void — Re-runs the highlight search based on the current searchText and caseSensitive values,
and makes the first match active.

The component also searches again by itself after its content changes.
- **setActive**(index: number, options?: HighlightNavigation): void — Moves the active highlight to the match at the specified zero-based index.

### [IgrIcon](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrIcon)
Shows an SVG icon from a collection of registered icons.

- **collection**: `string` — The registered collection to look the icon up in.
- **mirrored**: `boolean` — Whether the icon is flipped horizontally, for example for RTL layouts.
- **name**: `string` — The name of the icon glyph to draw.

### [IgrIconButton](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrIconButton)
A button that displays a single icon, designed for compact, icon-only
interactions such as toolbar actions, floating action buttons, or inline
controls.

The icon is sourced from the icon registry via the name and collection
attributes. Like the normal button, it can render as an anchor element when
href is set and is fully form-associated.

- **collection**: `string | undefined` — The collection the icon belongs to.
- **command**: `string | undefined` — The command to invoke on the target element specified by commandfor.
Part of the [Invoker Commands](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Invoker_Commands_API) API.
Custom commands must start with two dashes (e.g. '--my-command').
- **commandfor**: `string | null` — The ID of the target element for the invoker command.
Part of the [Invoker Commands API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Invoker_Commands_API).
- **commandForElement**: `Element | null` — The target element for the invoker command. Resolved from the `commandfor` ID.
- **disabled**: `boolean` — Whether the button is disabled. A disabled button ignores user interaction.
- **download**: `string | undefined` — Prompts the browser to download the linked resource rather than navigating
to it. The optional value is used as the suggested file name.
Only effective when href is set.
- **href**: `string | undefined` — The URL the button points to. When set, the component renders as an
<a> element instead of a <button>, enabling navigation on click.
Use together with target, download, and rel for full anchor semantics.
A disabled link renders a disabled <button> with the link role, because an
anchor has no disabled state.
- **mirrored**: `boolean` — Whether the icon is flipped horizontally. Use it for a directional icon
in a right-to-left layout.
- **name**: `string | undefined` — The name of the icon to display.
- **rel**: `string | undefined` — The relationship between the current document and the linked URL.
Accepts a space-separated list of link types (e.g. 'noopener noreferrer').
Only effective when href is set. When target="_blank" is used,
setting rel="noopener noreferrer" is strongly recommended for security.
- **target**: `"_blank" | "_parent" | "_self" | "_top" | undefined` — Where to open the linked document. Only effective when href is set.
- '_self' – current browsing context (default browser behavior).
- '_blank' – new tab or window.
- '_parent' – parent browsing context; falls back to _self if none.
- '_top' – top-level browsing context; falls back to _self if none.
- **type**: `"reset" | "submit" | "button"` — The type of the button, which determines its behavior and semantics.
- 'button' – no default action; useful for custom JavaScript handlers.
- 'submit' – submits the associated form when clicked.
- 'reset' – resets the associated form fields to their initial values.

Ignored when the button is rendered as a link (i.e. href is set).
- **variant**: `IconButtonVariant` — The variant of the button which determines its visual appearance.
- contained – filled background; highest visual emphasis (default).
- outlined – transparent background with a visible border.
- flat – no background or border; lowest visual emphasis.
- **form**: `any` — The `<form>` element the button is associated with.
Resolved through the standard form-association mechanism - either the
closest ancestor `<form>` or the form referenced by the button's `form`
attribute. Returns `null` when no form is associated.
Relevant only when `type` is `'submit'` or `'reset'`.
- **blur**(): void — Removes focus from the button.
- **click**(): void — Simulates a mouse click on the button, triggering its click handler and any associated form action.
- **focus**(options?: FocusOptions): void — Sets focus on the button.

### [IgrInput](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrInput)
A single-line text field to enter and edit data. It supports prefix and
suffix content, helper text, form integration and built-in validation.

- **autocomplete**: `string` — A hint for the browser on how to autofill the control.
- **autofocus**: `boolean` — Whether the control receives focus automatically.
- **inputMode**: `string` — A hint to the browser for which virtual keyboard layout to display.
See [relevant MDN article](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/inputmode)
- **label**: `string` — The label for the control.
- **max**: `number | undefined` — The maximum value the control accepts.
- **maxLength**: `number | undefined` — The maximum string length of the control.
- **min**: `number | undefined` — The minimum value the control accepts.
- **minLength**: `number | undefined` — The minimum string length required by the control.
- **outlined**: `boolean` — Whether the control has an outlined appearance.
- **pattern**: `string | undefined` — The regular expression the value is validated against.
- **placeholder**: `string` — The placeholder text of the control.
- **readOnly**: `boolean` — Whether the control is read-only.
- **step**: `number | undefined` — The granularity the value must adhere to.
- **type**: `InputType` — The type of the control.
- **validateOnly**: `boolean` — Whether the validation rules apply without restricting user input. The user can type past maxLength,
and the spin buttons of a number input can go past min and max.
- **value**: `string` — The value of the control.
- **selectionEnd**: `any` — The offset of the end of the text selection, in UTF-16 code units.
`null` before the first render and for the `email` and `number` types.
- **selectionStart**: `any` — The offset of the start of the text selection, in UTF-16 code units.
Equals `selectionEnd` when no text is selected. `null` before the first
render and for the `email` and `number` types, which have no selection.
- **blur**(): void — Removes focus from the control.
- **focus**(options?: FocusOptions): void — Sets focus on the control.
- **select**(): void — Selects all the text inside the input.
- **setRangeText**(replacement: string, start?: number, end?: number, selectMode?: RangeTextSelectMode): void — Replaces the text from start to end in the input. Without start and
end, replaces the selected text.
- **setSelectionRange**(start?: number, end?: number, direction?: SelectionRangeDirection): void — Sets the text selection range of the control.
- **stepDown**(n?: number): void — Decrements the numeric value of the input by one or more steps.
- **stepUp**(n?: number): void — Increments the numeric value of the input by one or more steps.

### [IgrLinearProgress](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrLinearProgress)
A linear progress indicator used to express unspecified wait time or display
the length of a process.

- **animationDuration**: `number` — The duration of the fill animation in milliseconds.
- **hideLabel**: `boolean` — Whether the default label is hidden.
- **indeterminate**: `boolean` — Whether the progress is indeterminate. An indeterminate progress has no
value and does not show the default label.
- **labelAlign**: `LinearProgressLabelAlign` — The position for the default label of the control.
- **labelFormat**: `string` — Format string for the default label of the control.
Placeholders:
 {0} - current value of the control.
 {1} - max value of the control.
- **max**: `number` — The maximum value of the control.
- **striped**: `boolean` — Whether the fill of the control is striped.
- **value**: `number` — The value of the control.
- **variant**: `StyleVariant` — The variant of the control.

### [IgrList](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrList)
Displays a collection of data items in a templatable list format.


### [IgrListHeader](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrListHeader)
Header list item.


### [IgrListItem](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrListItem)
The list-item component is a container
intended for row items in the list component.

- **selected**: `boolean` — Whether the list item is selected. It changes only the visual style of the
item.

### [IgrMaskInput](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrMaskInput)
An input field that restricts user input to a mask pattern and formats the visible value.

- **label**: `string` — The label for the control.
- **mask**: `string` — The mask pattern of the control.
- **outlined**: `boolean` — Whether the control has an outlined appearance.
- **placeholder**: `string` — The placeholder text of the control.
- **prompt**: `string` — The prompt symbol to use for unfilled parts of the mask pattern.
- **value**: `string` — The value of the control. Its format depends on `valueMode`.

An empty value is always an empty string, regardless of the value mode.
- **valueMode**: `MaskInputValueMode` — The format of the value and of the submitted form value:

- raw: The input without the mask literals and prompts (e.g. "5551234567")
- withFormatting: The input with the mask formatting (e.g. "(555) 123-4567")

An empty value is always an empty string, regardless of the value mode.
- **blur**(): void — Removes focus from the control.
- **focus**(options?: FocusOptions): void — Sets focus on the control.
- **isValidMaskPattern**(): boolean — Returns whether the current masked input is valid according to the mask pattern.
An empty control is valid. The required validator checks it.
- **select**(): void — Selects all the text inside the input.

### [IgrNavbar](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrNavbar)
A navigation bar component is used to facilitate navigation through
a series of hierarchical screens within an app.


### [IgrNavDrawer](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrNavDrawer)
A side navigation container that provides
quick access between views within an application.

The edge positions (start, end, top, bottom) render a modal <dialog>
with a focus trap and a backdrop. The relative position renders an inline
<nav> landmark.

Content in the mini slot renders a compact variant, which shows while the
drawer is closed.

The component integrates with the
[Invoker Commands API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Invoker_Commands_API):
an Ignite button or a native <button> with command="--show" / "--hide" / "--toggle"
and commandfor pointing to this element calls the corresponding method
declaratively without any JavaScript.

- **keepOpenOnEscape**: `boolean` — Whether the drawer stays open when the user presses Escape. Applies only to the
edge positions, because Escape does not close a relative drawer.
- **label**: `string | undefined` — The accessible label of the <dialog>, or of the <nav> landmark in the relative
position, and of the mini variant. Give each navigation landmark on a page a distinct label.
- **open**: `boolean` — Whether the drawer is open.
- **position**: `NavDrawerPosition` — The position of the drawer.

- start - anchored to the inline-start edge (default).
- end - anchored to the inline-end edge.
- top - anchored to the block-start edge.
- bottom - anchored to the block-end edge.
- relative - rendered inline within the page flow; no modal backdrop.
- **hide**(): Promise<boolean> — Closes the drawer. Returns true after the exit, or false when it is already closed or a
reopen ends the exit.
- **show**(): Promise<boolean> — Opens the drawer. Returns true on success, or false when it is already open.
- **toggle**(): Promise<boolean> — Toggles the open state of the drawer.

### [IgrNavDrawerHeaderItem](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrNavDrawerHeaderItem)
Represents a navigation drawer header item.


### [IgrNavDrawerItem](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrNavDrawerItem)
Represents a navigation drawer item.

- **active**: `boolean` — Whether the drawer item is active.
- **disabled**: `boolean` — Whether the drawer item is disabled.

### [IgrQrCode](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrQrCode)
Generates a QR code from a value and renders it as an SVG image.
Properties set the size, the shapes, the error correction level and an optional logo.

- **dotStyle**: `QrDotStyle` — The style of the data modules (dots) in the QR code, and of the inner dot of each finder-pattern
corner. This can be 'square', 'circle', or 'rounded'.
- **errorLevel**: `QrErrorCorrectionLevel` — The error correction level for the QR code, which determines the QR code's ability to be read if it is partially obscured or damaged.
Valid values are 'L', 'M', 'Q', and 'H', where 'L' provides the lowest level of error correction and 'H' provides the highest level.

When the level is not set, the code uses 'M'. A logo that is larger than the safe area of 'M'
raises the level to the smallest level that holds the logo. To restore this behavior, set
`undefined` or remove the attribute.
- **logoMargin**: `number | undefined` — The margin around the logo in pixels. This is the whitespace area surrounding the logo within the QR code,
which helps ensure that the logo does not interfere with the QR code's scannability.
- **logoSize**: `number` — The size of the logo, as a ratio of the maximum area that can safely be obscured by a logo
while the QR code remains scannable (up to 9% of the code's area, at the highest error
correction level). The value is a number from 0 to 1, where 0 means no logo and 1
means the logo covers the full safe area (not the entire QR code). Other values are clamped.
The default value is 0.4, meaning the logo covers 40% of that safe area (~3.6% of the QR code).

When error-level is not set and the logo is larger than the safe area of level 'M', the
component uses the smallest error correction level that holds the logo. When error-level
is set, the logo does not grow past the safe area of that level.
- **logoSrc**: `string | undefined` — The source URL of an optional logo image at the center of the QR code.
The component does not render a logo that fails to load, a javascript: or vbscript: URL,
or a data URI that is not an image.
- **margin**: `number` — The margin (quiet zone) around the QR code, expressed as a number of QR code modules rather
than pixels. This is the blank border area surrounding the code, which helps ensure that it
can be properly scanned.
- **size**: `number` — The size of the QR code in pixels. This determines the width and height of the generated QR code. The default value is 128 pixels.
- **squareStyle**: `QrCornerSquareStyle` — The style of the corner squares in the QR code. This can be 'square', 'circle', or 'rounded'.
- **value**: `string | undefined` — The value to encode in the QR code. This can be any string, such as a URL, text, or other data.
Without a value, the component renders nothing.
- **version**: `number | undefined` — The version of the QR code to generate, which determines the size and data capacity of the QR code.
Valid values are integers from 1 to 40, where each version corresponds to a specific module size and data capacity.

When it is not set, or it is not an integer from 1 to 40, the component selects the smallest
version that holds the value. When the value does not fit the version, the component renders nothing.
- **copyToClipboard**(options?: QrCodeCopyOptions): Promise<QrCodeCopyFormat> — Copies the QR code to the clipboard as an image and resolves to the format that the clipboard
received. A browser that cannot copy SVG gets only the PNG.

Browsers accept a clipboard write only in a focused document during a user action, so call
the method directly from the event handler, with no await before it.

Rejects when there is no value or it does not fit the version, when format is not
supported, when scale is not a positive finite number, when the image exceeds the maximum
canvas size, when the Clipboard API is not available, or when the browser refuses the write.
- **toBlob**(): Promise<Blob> — Serializes the QR code to an image/svg+xml blob.

Theme colors are resolved to plain fill attributes and a logo that is not a data URI
is fetched and inlined, so the blob renders identically outside the component.
A logo that cannot be fetched (for example a cross-origin URL without CORS headers) is omitted.

Rejects when there is no value or it does not fit the version.
- **toImage**(options?: QrCodeExportOptions): Promise<File> — Exports the QR code as an image file.

The scale option multiplies the size of the component: a 256px QR code exported
with scale: 2 produces a 512x512 image. When download is true the browser
download dialog opens for the file.

Rejects when there is no value or it does not fit the version, when format is not
supported, when scale is not a positive finite number, or when the resulting image
exceeds the maximum canvas size.

### [IgrRadio](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrRadio)
Lets the user select one option from a set. Radios with the same name
form a group, and only one radio of the group is checked.

- **checked**: `boolean` — Whether the control is checked. A checked radio clears the other radios
of its group.
- **labelPosition**: `ToggleLabelPosition` — The label position of the radio control.
- **required**: `boolean` — Whether the group of the radio is required. A required group fails
validation while none of its radios is checked.
- **value**: `string` — The value of the control, submitted when the control is checked.
- **blur**(): void — Removes focus from the radio control.
- **checkValidity**(): boolean — Checks the validity of the whole group. Each invalid radio of the group
emits invalid.
- **click**(): void — Simulates a click on the radio control.
- **focus**(options?: FocusOptions): void — Sets focus on the radio control.
- **reportValidity**(): boolean — Checks the validity of the group. An invalid radio emits invalid and
takes the focus. It shows its own validation messages, not the message of
the browser.
- **setCustomValidity**(message: string): void — Sets a custom validation message on every radio of the group. The radios
are invalid while message is not empty.

### [IgrRadioGroup](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrRadioGroup)
Unifies one or more radio components into a single group.

- **alignment**: `ContentOrientation` — Alignment of the radio controls inside this group.
- **defaultValue**: `string` — The value of the radio that is checked by default. A form reset checks
the radio with this value.
- **name**: `string` — The name applied to all radio buttons in the group.
- **value**: `string` — The value of the group, reflecting the value of the currently checked radio button.
Setting it checks the radio button in the group with a matching value.

### [IgrRangeSlider](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrRangeSlider)
A range slider component used to select two numeric values within a range.

- **disabled**: `boolean` — Whether the slider is disabled. A disabled slider ignores user interaction.
- **discreteTrack**: `boolean` — Whether the track shows the steps. It has no effect when step is 0.
- **hidePrimaryLabels**: `boolean` — Whether the labels of the primary ticks are hidden.
- **hideSecondaryLabels**: `boolean` — Whether the labels of the secondary ticks are hidden.
- **hideTooltip**: `boolean` — Whether the thumb tooltip is hidden.
- **locale**: `string` — The locale used to format the thumb and tick label values in the slider.
- **lower**: `number` — The current value of the lower thumb.
- **lowerBound**: `number` — The lower bound of the slider value. If not set, the `min` value is applied.
- **max**: `number` — The maximum value of the slider scale. Defaults to 100.

If `max` is less than `min`, the update keeps the previous `max`. The
update checks the values after all of them are set, so the order of the
attributes has no effect.

With slider labels in the default slot, `max` is always the number of
labels minus one.

If `upperBound` is greater than `max`, the slider uses `max` as the upper bound.
- **min**: `number` — The minimum value of the slider scale. Defaults to 0.

If `min` is greater than `max`, the update keeps the previous `min`. The
update checks the values after all of them are set, so the order of the
attributes has no effect.

With slider labels in the default slot, `min` is always 0.

If `lowerBound` is less than `min`, the slider uses `min` as the lower bound.
- **primaryTicks**: `number` — The number of primary ticks. It defaults to 0 which means no primary ticks are displayed.
- **secondaryTicks**: `number` — The number of secondary ticks between two primary ticks. Without primary
ticks, it is the total number of ticks. The default 0 shows no secondary ticks.
- **step**: `number` — The interval between two valid values, counted from `min`.

If set to 0 no stepping is implied and any value in the range is allowed.
A negative step is not valid, so the previous step stays.
With slider labels in the default slot, the step is always 1.
- **thumbLabelLower**: `string` — The accessible name of the lower thumb.
- **thumbLabelUpper**: `string` — The accessible name of the upper thumb.
- **tickLabelRotation**: `SliderTickLabelRotation` — The degrees for the rotation of the tick labels. Defaults to 0.
- **tickOrientation**: `SliderTickOrientation` — Where the ticks are drawn: before the track (start), after it (end),
or on both sides (mirror).
- **upper**: `number` — The current value of the upper thumb. Until it is set, and after the
attribute is removed, it follows `upperBound`.
- **upperBound**: `number` — The upper bound of the slider value. If not set, the `max` value is applied.
- **valueFormat**: `string | undefined` — String format used for the thumb and tick label values in the slider.
The {0} placeholder holds the formatted number.
- **valueFormatOptions**: `NumberFormatOptions | undefined` — Number format options used for the thumb and tick label values in the slider.
- **blur**(): void — Removes focus from the thumb.
- **disconnectedCallback**(): void — Invoked when the component is removed from the document's DOM.

This callback is the main signal to the element that it may no longer be
used. disconnectedCallback() should ensure that nothing is holding a
reference to the element (such as event listeners added to nodes external
to the element), so that it is free to be garbage collected.

disconnectedCallback() {
  super.disconnectedCallback();
  window.removeEventListener('keydown', this._handleKeydown);
}


An element may be re-connected after being disconnected.
- **focus**(options?: FocusOptions): void — Sets focus on the thumb, or on the lower thumb of a range slider. A thumb
that has the focus keeps it. A disabled slider does not take the focus.

### [IgrRating](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrRating)
A rating component that allows users to view and provide ratings using customizable symbols.
It supports fractional values, hover previews, keyboard navigation, single-selection mode,
and integrates with forms as a number input.

- **allowReset**: `boolean` — Whether to reset the rating when the user selects the same value.
- **hoverPreview**: `boolean` — Whether to show a preview of the value when hovering over the symbols.
- **label**: `string | undefined` — The label of the control.
- **max**: `number` — The maximum value for the rating.

With projected symbols, the maximum value is the number of symbols. A
maximum below the value also lowers the value.
- **readOnly**: `boolean` — Whether the rating is read-only. A read-only rating shows its value but
ignores user input.
- **single**: `boolean` — Whether only the symbol at the value is full, instead of all symbols up
to it. It also sets step to 1 and rounds the value up.
- **step**: `number` — The minimum value change allowed.

Valid values are in the interval between 0.001 and 1 inclusive.
The component clamps a value outside of the interval to the closest bound.
In single selection mode, the step is always 1.
- **value**: `number` — The value of the rating, clamped between 0 and `max`.
- **valueFormat**: `string | undefined` — The format of the aria-valuetext of the rating. {0} stands for the
value and {1} for the maximum value.

Use it for screen readers and for localization.
- **blur**(): void — Removes focus from the rating.
- **focus**(options?: FocusOptions): void — Sets focus on the rating. A disabled rating does not take the focus.
- **stepDown**(n?: number): void — Decrements the value of the control by n steps multiplied by
the step factor.
- **stepUp**(n?: number): void — Increments the value of the control by n steps multiplied by the
step factor.

### [IgrRatingSymbol](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrRatingSymbol)
A custom symbol for the rating. Put the full symbol in the default slot and
the empty symbol in the empty slot.

- **connectedCallback**(): void — Invoked when the component is added to the document's DOM.

In connectedCallback() you should setup tasks that should only occur when
the element is connected to the document. The most common of these is
adding event listeners to nodes external to the element, like a keydown
event handler added to the window.

connectedCallback() {
  super.connectedCallback();
  addEventListener('keydown', this._handleKeydown);
}


Typically, anything done in connectedCallback() should be undone when the
element is disconnected, in disconnectedCallback().

### [IgrRipple](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrRipple)
Shows a ripple wave on a pointer press, to mark an element as an
interactive surface.


### [IgrSelect](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrSelect)
Represents a control that provides a menu of options.

- **autofocus**: `boolean` — Whether the control takes the focus after its first render.
- **distance**: `number` — The distance of the select dropdown from its input.
- **keepOpenOnOutsideClick**: `boolean` — Whether the component stays open when the user clicks outside of it.
- **keepOpenOnSelect**: `boolean` — Whether the component stays open after the user selects an item.
- **label**: `string` — The label of the control.
- **open**: `boolean` — Whether the component is open.
- **outlined**: `boolean` — Whether the control has an outlined appearance.
- **placeholder**: `string` — The placeholder text of the control.
- **placement**: `PopoverPlacement` — The preferred placement of the select dropdown around its input.
- **scrollStrategy**: `PopoverScrollStrategy` — The behavior of the component when a parent container scrolls.

If the value is hide, the component hides while the anchor is fully out
of view. hide is the default value.

If the value is scroll, the component stays visible and anchored.

If the value is close, the component closes on each scroll.
- **value**: `string | undefined` — The value of the control.
- **groups**: `any` — Returns the groups of the select component.
- **items**: `any` — Returns the items of the select component.
- **selectedItem**: `any` — Returns the selected item from the dropdown or null.
- **blur**(): void — Removes focus from the component.
- **clearSelection**(): void — Resets the current value and selection of the component.
- **focus**(options?: FocusOptions): void — Sets focus on the component.
- **hide**(): Promise<boolean> — Closes the component. It does not emit events. The promise resolves to
false when the component is already closed, or when a later call
replaces this one.
- **navigateTo**(value: string): IgcSelectItemComponent | null — Navigates to the item with the specified value. If it exists, returns the found item, otherwise - null.
- **navigateTo**(index: number): IgcSelectItemComponent | null — Navigates to the item at the specified index. If it exists, returns the found item, otherwise - null.
- **select**(value: string): IgcSelectItemComponent | null — Selects the item with the specified value. If it exists, returns the found item, otherwise - null.
- **select**(index: number): IgcSelectItemComponent | null — Selects the item at the specified index. If it exists, returns the found item, otherwise - null.
- **show**(): Promise<boolean> — Opens the component. It does not emit events. The promise resolves to
false when the component is already open, or when a later call replaces
this one.
- **toggle**(): Promise<boolean> — Opens the component when it is closed, and closes it when it is open. It
does not emit events. The promise resolves to true when the state
changes.

### [IgrSelectGroup](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrSelectGroup)
A container for a group of select items.

- **disabled**: `boolean` — Whether the group and all its children are disabled.
- **items**: `IgcSelectItemComponent[]` — All child select items.

### [IgrSelectHeader](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrSelectHeader)
Represents a header item in a select component.


### [IgrSelectItem](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrSelectItem)
Represents an item in a select list.

- **active**: `boolean` — Whether the item is active. The active item is the target of keyboard
navigation and the only item in the tab order.
- **active**: `boolean` — Whether the item is active. The active item has the visual focus during
keyboard navigation.
- **disabled**: `boolean` — Whether the item is disabled.
- **selected**: `boolean` — Whether the item is selected. A change also sets active to the same
value.
- **value**: `string` — The value of the item. Falls back to the text content of the element.

### [IgrSlider](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrSlider)
A slider component used to select a numeric value within a range.

- **disabled**: `boolean` — Whether the slider is disabled. A disabled slider ignores user interaction.
- **discreteTrack**: `boolean` — Whether the track shows the steps. It has no effect when step is 0.
- **hidePrimaryLabels**: `boolean` — Whether the labels of the primary ticks are hidden.
- **hideSecondaryLabels**: `boolean` — Whether the labels of the secondary ticks are hidden.
- **hideTooltip**: `boolean` — Whether the thumb tooltip is hidden.
- **locale**: `string` — The locale used to format the thumb and tick label values in the slider.
- **lowerBound**: `number` — The lower bound of the slider value. If not set, the `min` value is applied.
- **max**: `number` — The maximum value of the slider scale. Defaults to 100.

If `max` is less than `min`, the update keeps the previous `max`. The

With slider labels in the default slot, `max` is always the number of

- **min**: `number` — The minimum value of the slider scale. Defaults to 0.

If `min` is greater than `max`, the update keeps the previous `min`. The

attributes has no effect.

With slider labels in the default slot, `min` is always 0.

If `lowerBound` is less than `min`, the slider uses `min` as the lower bound.

- **secondaryTicks**: `number` — The number of secondary ticks between two primary ticks. Without primary

If set to 0 no stepping is implied and any value in the range is allowed.

- **upperBound**: `number` — The upper bound of the slider value. If not set, the `max` value is applied.

disconnectedCallback() {
  super.disconnectedCallback();
  window.removeEventListener('keydown', this._handleKeydown);
}


An element may be re-connected after being disconnected.
- **focus**(options?: FocusOptions): void — Sets focus on the thumb, or on the lower thumb of a range slider. A thumb
that has the focus keeps it. A disabled slider does not take the focus.
- **stepDown**(stepDecrement?: number): void — Decrements the value of the slider by stepDecrement * step, where stepDecrement defaults to 1.
- **stepUp**(stepIncrement?: number): void — Increments the value of the slider by stepIncrement * step, where stepIncrement defaults to 1.

### [IgrSliderLabel](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrSliderLabel)
Allows formatting the values of the slider as string values.
The text content of the slider labels is used for thumb and tick labels.


### [IgrSnackbar](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrSnackbar)
Shows a brief message about an operation, with an optional action.

The component supports the
[Invoker Commands API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Invoker_Commands_API).
A button with command="--show", "--hide" or "--toggle" and a
commandfor that points to this element calls the matching method.

- **actionText**: `string | undefined` — The text of the action button.
- **displayTime**: `number` — The time in milliseconds that the component stays visible. The time
stops while the pointer or the keyboard focus is in the component, and
starts again from the full value when both leave. A value of 0 or less
keeps the component open.
- **keepOpen**: `boolean` — Whether the component stays open after the displayTime is over.
- **open**: `boolean` — Whether the component is open.

Setting it skips the fade. Use the show(), hide() and toggle()
methods for a fade.
- **position**: `AbsolutePosition` — The position of the component in the viewport or in the container.
- **positioning**: `NotificationPositioning` — The positioning strategy of the component.

viewport - positions against the viewport, ignoring every ancestor.
container - positions inside the bounding box of the closest visible
ancestor, at the place that position sets.
- **connectedCallback**(): void — Invoked when the component is added to the document's DOM.

In connectedCallback() you should setup tasks that should only occur when
the element is connected to the document. The most common of these is
adding event listeners to nodes external to the element, like a keydown
event handler added to the window.

connectedCallback() {
  super.connectedCallback();
  addEventListener('keydown', this._handleKeydown);
}


Typically, anything done in connectedCallback() should be undone when the
element is disconnected, in disconnectedCallback().
- **disconnectedCallback**(): void — Invoked when the component is removed from the document's DOM.

This callback is the main signal to the element that it may no longer be
used. disconnectedCallback() should ensure that nothing is holding a
reference to the element (such as event listeners added to nodes external
to the element), so that it is free to be garbage collected.

disconnectedCallback() {
  super.disconnectedCallback();
  window.removeEventListener('keydown', this._handleKeydown);
}


An element may be re-connected after being disconnected.
- **hide**(): Promise<boolean> — Closes the component. Resolves to false when it is already closed or
fades out, or when open is set to false and then to true during the
fade-out.
- **show**(): Promise<boolean> — Opens the component, also during the fade-out of hide(). When it is
already open, the display time starts again, and the promise resolves to
false. It also resolves to false when container positioning finds no
visible ancestor, or when open is set to false during the fade-in.
- **toggle**(): Promise<boolean> — Opens the component when it is closed, and closes it when it is open.
Resolves to true when the state changes.

### [IgrSplitter](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrSplitter)
A splitter component that provides a resizable split-pane layout, dividing the view
into two panels - *start* and *end* - separated by a draggable bar.

Panels can be resized by dragging the bar, using keyboard shortcuts, or collapsed/expanded
using the built-in collapse buttons or the programmatic toggle() API.
Nested splitters are supported for more complex layouts.

## Keyboard interactions

When the splitter bar is focused:

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Arrow Left / Arrow Right | Resize panes (horizontal orientation) |
| Arrow Up / Arrow Down | Resize panes (vertical orientation) |
| Home | Snap start pane to its minimum size |
| End | Snap start pane to its maximum size |
| Ctrl + Arrow Left / Ctrl + Arrow Up | Expand the end pane if it is collapsed, else toggle the start pane |
| Ctrl + Arrow Right / Ctrl + Arrow Down | Expand the start pane if it is collapsed, else toggle the end pane |

In a right-to-left context, Arrow Left and Arrow Right swap their actions.

- **disableCollapse**: `boolean` — Whether collapsing either pane is disabled. When true, this also hides
the expand/collapse buttons on the splitter bar.
- **disableResize**: `boolean` — Whether resizing the panes by dragging the splitter bar or using keyboard
shortcuts is disabled. When true, this also hides the drag handle on the
splitter bar.
- **endCollapsed**: `boolean` — Whether the end pane is currently collapsed. Set this property to
collapse or expand the pane programmatically.
- **endMaxSize**: `string | undefined` — The maximum size of the end pane.

Accepts a CSS length with an explicit unit, e.g. 500px or 80%, or a
unitless 0. Setting auto, any other unitless or unparsable value, a
negative value, or a percentage above 100 removes the constraint.
- **endMinSize**: `string | undefined` — The minimum size of the end pane.

Accepts a CSS length with an explicit unit, e.g. 100px or 20%, or a
unitless 0. Setting auto, any other unitless or unparsable value, a
negative value, or a percentage above 100 removes the constraint.
- **endSize**: `string | undefined` — The size of the end pane.

Accepts a CSS length with an explicit unit, e.g. `200px` or `50%`, or a
unitless `0`. Setting `auto`, any other unitless or unparsable value, a
negative value, or a percentage above 100 falls back to automatic sizing.
- **hideCollapseButtons**: `boolean` — Whether the expand/collapse buttons on the splitter bar are hidden.

The buttons are also hidden when disable-collapse is true. While a pane
is collapsed, only its expand button shows.
- **hideDragHandle**: `boolean` — Whether the drag handle on the splitter bar is hidden.

The drag handle is also hidden when disable-resize is true.
- **locale**: `string`
- **orientation**: `SplitterOrientation` — The orientation of the splitter, which determines the direction of resizing and collapsing.

Changing the orientation after the initial render returns the panes to the
sizes set through startSize and endSize, or to automatic sizing. The
sizes from a drag, a key press or a collapse were measured on the other
axis, so they are dropped. The minimum and maximum sizes stay.
- **resourceStrings**: `TGet`
- **startCollapsed**: `boolean` — Whether the start pane is currently collapsed. Set this property to
collapse or expand the pane programmatically.
- **startMaxSize**: `string | undefined` — The maximum size of the start pane.

Accepts a CSS length with an explicit unit, e.g. 500px or 80%, or a
unitless 0. Setting auto, any other unitless or unparsable value, a
negative value, or a percentage above 100 removes the constraint.
- **startMinSize**: `string | undefined` — The minimum size of the start pane.

Accepts a CSS length with an explicit unit, e.g. 100px or 20%, or a
unitless 0. Setting auto, any other unitless or unparsable value, a
negative value, or a percentage above 100 removes the constraint.
- **startSize**: `string | undefined` — The size of the start pane.

Accepts a CSS length with an explicit unit, e.g. `200px` or `50%`, or a
unitless `0`. Setting `auto`, any other unitless or unparsable value, a
negative value, or a percentage above 100 falls back to automatic sizing.
- **disconnectedCallback**(): void — Invoked when the component is removed from the document's DOM.

This callback is the main signal to the element that it may no longer be
used. disconnectedCallback() should ensure that nothing is holding a
reference to the element (such as event listeners added to nodes external
to the element), so that it is free to be garbage collected.

disconnectedCallback() {
  super.disconnectedCallback();
  window.removeEventListener('keydown', this._handleKeydown);
}


An element may be re-connected after being disconnected.
- **toggle**(position: PanePosition): void — Toggles the collapsed state of the specified pane.

Does not emit igcLayoutChanged - that event reports user-driven changes,
and a programmatic call is already known to the caller.

### [IgrStep](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrStep)
A step component used within a stepper to represent an individual step in a wizard-like workflow.

- **active**: `boolean` — Whether the step is active.

Active steps are styled with an active state and their content is visible.
Setting it activates the step at once, also a disabled step, so of several
steps set in one task, the last one is active.
- **complete**: `boolean` — Whether the step is completed.
- **disabled**: `boolean` — Whether the step is disabled.

Disabled steps are styled with a disabled state and are not interactive.
- **invalid**: `boolean` — Whether the step is invalid.

A visited step that is not active shows an error state. In linear mode,
the user cannot open the steps after an invalid step.
- **optional**: `boolean` — Whether the step is optional.

In linear mode, an invalid optional step does not block the steps after it.

### [IgrStepper](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrStepper)
A stepper component that provides a wizard-like workflow by dividing content into logical steps.

- **animationDuration**: `number` — The animation duration in either vertical or horizontal mode in milliseconds.
- **contentTop**: `boolean` — Whether the content is displayed above the steps. Applies only to the
horizontal orientation.
- **horizontalAnimation**: `HorizontalTransitionAnimation` — The animation type when in horizontal mode.
- **linear**: `boolean` — Whether the stepper is linear.
- **orientation**: `StepperOrientation` — The orientation of the stepper.
- **stepType**: `StepperStepType` — The visual type of the steps.
- **titlePosition**: `StepperTitlePosition` — The position of the steps title.
- **verticalAnimation**: `StepperVerticalAnimation` — The animation type when in vertical mode.
- **steps**: `any` — The steps of the stepper.
- **navigateTo**(index: number): void — Activates the step at a given index. Does nothing for a disabled step.
- **next**(): void — Activates the next enabled step.
- **prev**(): void — Activates the previous enabled step.
- **reset**(): void — Resets the stepper to its initial state and activates the first enabled step.

### [IgrSwitch](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrSwitch)
Similar to a checkbox, a switch controls the state of a single setting on or off.

- **checked**: `boolean` — Whether the control is checked.
- **labelPosition**: `ToggleLabelPosition` — The label position of the control.
- **value**: `string` — The value of the control, submitted when the control is checked.
- **blur**(): void — Removes focus from the control.
- **click**(): void — Simulates a click on the control.
- **focus**(options?: FocusOptions): void — Sets focus on the control.

### [IgrTab](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrTab)
A tab nested in a tabs component. Find-in-page, a text fragment or a link to
an element in the panel of a tab that is not disabled selects it.

- **disabled**: `boolean` — Whether the tab is disabled.
- **href**: `string | undefined` — The URL of the tab. When set, the tab header renders as a link.

A plain click selects the tab and follows the link; cancel igcNavigate to route
on the client. A click with a modifier key or the middle button opens the link
without selecting the tab. A disabled tab does not follow its link.
- **label**: `string` — The tab item label.
- **rel**: `string | undefined` — Space-separated link types, used when href is set.
- **selected**: `boolean` — Whether the tab is selected.
- **target**: `"_blank" | "_parent" | "_self" | "_top" | undefined` — Where to open the URL when href is set. Without it, the target of the page's
<base> element applies. A target other than _self never changes the selection.
In a page that is not in a frame, _parent and _top count as _self.

### [IgrTabs](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrTabs)
Tabs organize and allow navigation between groups of content that are related and at the same level of hierarchy.

- **activation**: `TabsActivation` — The activation behavior of the tabs.

With auto, a tab is selected when it receives keyboard focus.
With manual, a tab is selected only on click, or on Enter or Space.
- **alignment**: `TabsAlignment` — The alignment of the tab headers in the header strip.

In a column, start is the top and end is the bottom.
- **headerPosition**: `TabsHeaderPosition` — The side of the panels on which the tab headers are placed.

With top, the headers form a row above the panels. With start and end, they
form a column before or after the panels in the text direction, so start is on
the right in a right-to-left layout. In a column, the Up and Down arrow keys move
between the tabs. When the headers do not fit in the height of the tabs, scroll
buttons above and below them scroll the column.
- **selected**: `any` — The label of the selected tab, or its `id` when the tab has no label.
An empty string when no tab is selected.
- **selectedTab**: `any` — The selected tab, or `null` when no tab is selected.
- **tabs**: `any` — The tab children of the component.
- **select**(idOrLabel: string): void — Selects the tab matching the passed IDREF or label and displays the corresponding panel.

Disabled tabs and values not matching any tab are ignored.
- **select**(ref: IgcTabComponent): void — Selects the passed tab and displays the corresponding panel.

A disabled tab, or a tab that is not a child of the component, is ignored.

### [IgrTextarea](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrTextarea)
A multi-line plain-text field for a large amount of free-form text,
for example a comment in a review or feedback form.

- **autocapitalize**: `string` — Whether and how the browser capitalizes the text that the user enters.

[MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/autocapitalize).
- **autocomplete**: `string` — A hint for the browser on how to autofill the control.
Refer to [this page](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/autocomplete) for additional information.
- **inputMode**: `string` — A hint to the browser for which virtual keyboard layout to display.

[MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/inputmode)
- **label**: `string` — The label for the control.
- **maxLength**: `number` — The maximum number of characters (UTF-16 code units) that the user can enter.
If this value isn't specified, the user can enter an unlimited number of characters.
- **minLength**: `number` — The minimum number of characters (UTF-16 code units) that the value must have.
- **outlined**: `boolean` — Whether the control has an outlined appearance.
- **placeholder**: `string` — The placeholder text of the control.
- **readOnly**: `boolean` — Whether the control is read-only.
- **resize**: `TextareaResize` — How the user can resize the control.
With auto, the height of the control fits its content and the resize handle is hidden.
- **rows**: `number` — The number of visible text lines of the control. As in the native textarea, a value
less than 1 shows 2 lines.
- **spellcheck**: `boolean` — Whether the browser checks the spelling of the value. As for the native attribute,
only the "false" attribute value turns the check off.
- **validateOnly**: `boolean` — Whether the validation rules apply without restricting user input. The user can type past maxLength.
- **value**: `string` — The value of the component.
- **wrap**: `"off" | "hard" | "soft"` — How the control wraps long lines of text. With off, the lines do not wrap.
Unlike the native element, hard does not add line breaks to the submitted value.
Refer to [this page on MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/textarea#attributes)
for explanation of the available values.
- **selectionEnd**: `any` — The offset of the end of the text selection, in UTF-16 code units.
- **selectionStart**: `any` — The offset of the start of the text selection, in UTF-16 code units.
Equals `selectionEnd` when no text is selected.
- **blur**(): void — Removes focus from the control.
- **focus**(options?: FocusOptions): void — Sets focus on the control.
- **scrollTo**(options?: ScrollToOptions): void — Scrolls the text of the control to the given position.
- **scrollTo**(x: number, y: number): void — Scrolls the text of the control to the given x and y coordinates.
- **select**(): void — Selects all text within the control.
- **setRangeText**(replacement: string, start?: number, end?: number, selectMode?: RangeTextSelectMode): void — Replaces the text from start to end in the control. Without start and
end, replaces the selected text.
- **setSelectionRange**(start: number, end: number, direction?: SelectionRangeDirection): void — Sets the text selection range of the control.

### [IgrThemeProvider](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrThemeProvider)
Provides a theme to its descendant components through Lit context.

Use it to scope a theme to a part of the page. The library components in
the provider use its theme instead of the global theme.

- **theme**: `"material" | "bootstrap" | "indigo" | "fluent"` — The theme to provide to descendant components.
- **variant**: `"light" | "dark"` — The theme variant to provide to descendant components.

### [IgrTile](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrTile)
The tile component is used within the tile manager as a container
for displaying various types of information.

- **colSpan**: `number` — The number of columns the tile spans. A value is truncated to a whole
number, at least 1. The tile spans at most the columns from its start to
the last column, and the value stays.
- **colStart**: `number | null` — The start column of the tile. A value below 1 removes the explicit start.
A start after the last column moves the tile back so that its span fits,
and the value stays. A resize that changes the column span of such a tile
sets the start to the column where the tile is.
- **disableFullscreen**: `boolean` — Whether to hide the fullscreen-action slot and the default fullscreen
action.
- **disableMaximize**: `boolean` — Whether to hide the maximize-action slot and the default maximize action.
- **disableResize**: `boolean` — Whether to disable resizing of the tile, whatever the resize mode of the
manager.
- **locale**: `string`
- **maximized**: `boolean` — Whether the tile occupies all available space within the layout.
- **position**: `number` — The visual position of the tile in the layout, as the CSS order. A value
is truncated to a whole number.
- **resourceStrings**: `TGet`
- **rowSpan**: `number` — The number of rows the tile spans. A value is truncated to a whole
number, at least 1.
- **rowStart**: `number | null` — The start row of the tile. A value below 1 removes the explicit start.
- **fullscreen**: `any` — Whether the tile occupies the whole screen.

### [IgrTileManager](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrTileManager)
The tile manager component enables the dynamic arrangement, resizing, and interaction of tiles.

- **columnCount**: `number` — The number of columns, truncated to a whole number. A value of 0 or less
gives a responsive layout.
- **dragMode**: `TileManagerDragMode` — The drag mode of the tiles. none turns drag and drop off.
- **gap**: `string | undefined` — The gap between the tiles.
- **locale**: `string` — The locale of the tiles. A tile without its own locale takes this one.
Without it, the manager takes its own `lang`, else the locale of the
nearest ancestor that has a `locale` (a component) or a `lang`, and then
the global locale.
- **minColumnWidth**: `string | undefined` — The minimum width of a column.
- **minRowHeight**: `string | undefined` — The minimum height of a row.
- **resizeMode**: `TileManagerResizeMode` — The resize mode of the tiles. none turns resizing off.
- **tiles**: `any` — The tiles, sorted by their position in the layout.
- **loadLayout**(data: string): void — Applies a layout from saveLayout to the tiles with the same id. Invalid JSON throws.
- **saveLayout**(): string — Returns the tile properties as a JSON string. The content of the tiles is not saved.

### [IgrToast](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrToast)
Shows a brief, non-interactive notification.

The component supports the
[Invoker Commands API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Invoker_Commands_API).
A button with command="--show", "--hide" or "--toggle" and a
commandfor that points to this element calls the matching method.

- **displayTime**: `number` — The time in milliseconds that the component stays visible. The time
stops while the pointer or the keyboard focus is in the component, and
starts again from the full value when both leave. A value of 0 or less
keeps the component open.
- **keepOpen**: `boolean` — Whether the component stays open after the displayTime is over.
- **open**: `boolean` — Whether the component is open.

Setting it skips the fade. Use the show(), hide() and toggle()
methods for a fade.
- **position**: `AbsolutePosition` — The position of the component in the viewport or in the container.
- **positioning**: `NotificationPositioning` — The positioning strategy of the component.

viewport - positions against the viewport, ignoring every ancestor.
container - positions inside the bounding box of the closest visible
ancestor, at the place that position sets.
- **connectedCallback**(): void — Invoked when the component is added to the document's DOM.

In connectedCallback() you should setup tasks that should only occur when
the element is connected to the document. The most common of these is
adding event listeners to nodes external to the element, like a keydown
event handler added to the window.

connectedCallback() {
  super.connectedCallback();
  addEventListener('keydown', this._handleKeydown);
}


Typically, anything done in connectedCallback() should be undone when the
element is disconnected, in disconnectedCallback().
- **disconnectedCallback**(): void — Invoked when the component is removed from the document's DOM.

This callback is the main signal to the element that it may no longer be
used. disconnectedCallback() should ensure that nothing is holding a
reference to the element (such as event listeners added to nodes external
to the element), so that it is free to be garbage collected.

disconnectedCallback() {
  super.disconnectedCallback();
  window.removeEventListener('keydown', this._handleKeydown);
}


An element may be re-connected after being disconnected.
- **hide**(): Promise<boolean> — Closes the component. Resolves to false when it is already closed or
fades out, or when open is set to false and then to true during the
fade-out.
- **show**(): Promise<boolean> — Opens the component, also during the fade-out of hide(). When it is
already open, the display time starts again, and the promise resolves to
false. It also resolves to false when container positioning finds no
visible ancestor, or when open is set to false during the fade-in.
- **toggle**(): Promise<boolean> — Opens the component when it is closed, and closes it when it is open.
Resolves to true when the state changes.

### [IgrToggleButton](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrToggleButton)
The toggle button wraps a native button element and exposes additional value and selected properties.
Use it in a button group to make a toolbar or a set of options.

- **disabled**: `boolean` — Whether the button is disabled.
- **selected**: `boolean` — Whether the button is selected.
- **value**: `string` — The value of the control.
- **blur**(): void — Removes focus from the button.
- **click**(): void — Simulates a mouse click on the element.
- **disconnectedCallback**(): void — Invoked when the component is removed from the document's DOM.

This callback is the main signal to the element that it may no longer be
used. disconnectedCallback() should ensure that nothing is holding a
reference to the element (such as event listeners added to nodes external
to the element), so that it is free to be garbage collected.

disconnectedCallback() {
  super.disconnectedCallback();
  window.removeEventListener('keydown', this._handleKeydown);
}


An element may be re-connected after being disconnected.
- **focus**(options?: FocusOptions): void — Sets focus on the button.

### [IgrTooltip](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrTooltip)
Shows supplementary information about an element when the user interacts with it, for example on hover or focus.
It supports custom placement, delays, a sticky mode and animations.

- **anchor**: `string | Element | undefined` — An element instance or an IDREF to use as the anchor for the tooltip.
- **hideDelay**: `number` — The time in milliseconds before a hide trigger closes the tooltip.
A negative value is the same as 0.
- **hideTriggers**: `string` — The anchor events that hide the tooltip.
A list of event names, separated by commas or spaces.
- **locale**: `string`
- **message**: `string` — The plain-text content of the tooltip. Slotted content replaces it.
- **offset**: `number` — The offset of the tooltip from the anchor in pixels.
- **open**: `boolean` — Whether the tooltip is showing.
- **placement**: `PopoverPlacement` — Where to place the tooltip relative to its anchor element.
- **resourceStrings**: `TGet`
- **scrollStrategy**: `PopoverScrollStrategy` — The behavior of the tooltip when an ancestor scroll container scrolls.

If the value is hide, the tooltip hides while the anchor is fully out
of view. hide is the default value.

If the value is scroll, the tooltip stays visible and anchored.

If the value is close, the tooltip closes on each scroll, also in
sticky mode. The Escape key also closes a sticky tooltip.
- **showDelay**: `number` — The time in milliseconds before a show trigger opens the tooltip.
A negative value is the same as 0.
- **showTriggers**: `string` — The anchor events that show the tooltip.
A list of event names, separated by commas or spaces.
- **sticky**: `boolean` — Whether the tooltip stays visible until the user closes it with the close button or the Escape key.
- **withArrow**: `boolean` — Whether to render an arrow indicator for the tooltip.
- **hide**(): Promise<boolean> — Hides the tooltip if not already hidden.
- **show**(target?: string | Element): Promise<boolean> — Shows the tooltip if not already showing.
If a target is provided, sets it as a transient anchor.
- **showAt**(rect: TooltipRect): Promise<boolean> — Shows the tooltip at a point or against a rectangle, in viewport
coordinates, for example at the clientX and clientY of a pointer event.
Without width and height, the rectangle is a point.
- **toggle**(): Promise<boolean> — Toggles the tooltip between shown/hidden state.

### [IgrTree](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrTree)
The tree allows users to represent hierarchical data in a tree-view structure,
maintaining parent-child relationships, as well as to define static tree-view structure without a corresponding data model.

- **locale**: `string`
- **resourceStrings**: `TGet`
- **selection**: `TreeSelection` — The selection mode of the tree. A change clears the current selection.
- **singleBranchExpand**: `boolean` — Whether only one branch of the tree can be expanded at a time. When the user
expands an item, the items outside its path collapse.
- **toggleNodeOnClick**: `boolean` — Whether a click on an item toggles its expanded state.
- **items**: `any` — All items of the tree, in document order. Empty during server-side rendering.
- **collapse**(items?: IgcTreeItemComponent[]): void — Collapses all of the passed items.
If no items are passed, collapses ALL items.
- **connectedCallback**(): void — Invoked when the component is added to the document's DOM.

In connectedCallback() you should setup tasks that should only occur when
the element is connected to the document. The most common of these is
adding event listeners to nodes external to the element, like a keydown
event handler added to the window.

connectedCallback() {
  super.connectedCallback();
  addEventListener('keydown', this._handleKeydown);
}


Typically, anything done in connectedCallback() should be undone when the
element is disconnected, in disconnectedCallback().
- **deselect**(items?: IgcTreeItemComponent[]): void — Deselects the passed items. Without an argument, deselects all items. Emits no event.
- **expand**(items?: IgcTreeItemComponent[]): void — Expands all of the passed items.
If no items are passed, expands ALL items.
- **select**(items?: IgcTreeItemComponent[]): void — Selects the passed items. Without an argument, selects all items. Emits no event.

### [IgrTreeItem](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrTreeItem)
The tree-item component represents a child item of the tree component or another tree item.
Find-in-page, a text fragment or a link to an element in the children of a
collapsed item expands it.

- **active**: `boolean` — Whether the item is the active item of the tree. When true, the ancestors of
the item expand.
- **disabled**: `boolean` — Whether the tree item is disabled. A disabled item does not respond to user interaction.
- **expanded**: `boolean` — Whether the tree item is expanded.
- **label**: `string` — The tree item label.
- **level**: `number` — The depth of the item, relative to the root.
- **loading**: `boolean` — Whether the item is loading data, for load-on-demand scenarios. The item
shows a loading indicator in place of the expand indicator.
- **parent**: `IgcTreeItemComponent | null` — The parent item of the current tree item (if any)
- **selected**: `boolean` — Whether the tree item is selected.
- **value**: `any` — The value that the tree item represents. The component does not use it.
- **path**: `any` — The full path to the tree item, starting from the top-most ancestor.
- **tree**: `any` — A reference to the tree the item is a part of.
- **collapse**(): void — Collapses the tree item.
- **connectedCallback**(): void — Invoked when the component is added to the document's DOM.

In connectedCallback() you should setup tasks that should only occur when
the element is connected to the document. The most common of these is
adding event listeners to nodes external to the element, like a keydown
event handler added to the window.

connectedCallback() {
  super.connectedCallback();
  addEventListener('keydown', this._handleKeydown);
}


Typically, anything done in connectedCallback() should be undone when the
element is disconnected, in disconnectedCallback().
- **disconnectedCallback**(): void — Invoked when the component is removed from the document's DOM.

This callback is the main signal to the element that it may no longer be
used. disconnectedCallback() should ensure that nothing is holding a
reference to the element (such as event listeners added to nodes external
to the element), so that it is free to be garbage collected.

disconnectedCallback() {
  super.disconnectedCallback();
  window.removeEventListener('keydown', this._handleKeydown);
}


An element may be re-connected after being disconnected.
- **expand**(): void — Expands the tree item.
- **getChildren**(options?: any): IgcTreeItemComponent[] — Returns the child items. With flatten: true it returns all the
descendant items, otherwise only the direct children.
- **toggle**(): void — Toggles tree item expansion state.

### [IgrVirtualScroll](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/classes/IgrVirtualScroll)
A virtual scroll component for large lists. Only the items visible in the
viewport are rendered.

The component renders into its light DOM, so ::part() does not apply to its
parts. Select them with attribute selectors, such as [part~="virtualization-track"].

- **data**: `T[]` — The array of items to virtualize.

Compared by reference: a mutation in place (data.push(...)) causes no
update. Assign a new array instead. The igcDataRequest flow also
expects a new array.
- **estimatedItemSize**: `number` — Estimated item size in pixels, used before an item is measured in the DOM.
After the first render of an item, the engine replaces the estimate with the measured size.
The average measured size also replaces the estimate of the items that are not measured
yet, so the scrollbar follows the real content.
- **itemTemplate**: `VirtualScrollItemTemplate<T> | null` — A function that renders each item in the virtual scroll list.
Receives a VirtualScrollItemContext<T> with the item data, its index, and the total count.
Without it, nothing is rendered.

Items are measured by their border box, so margins accumulate as drift
down the list. Use padding on the item, or a gap on a wrapper, instead.

Only the current window is in the DOM, so assistive technology cannot
infer an item's position from the markup. In a template that renders a
role with set semantics (option, listitem, row, ...), map the
context's index and count to aria-posinset and aria-setsize.

Item elements are recycled (see keyFunction), so DOM state that the
template does not bind moves to another item, for example the state of a
checkbox without a checked binding. Bind all item state. Lit compares a
binding with the value that it set last, not with the element, so bind
state that the user changes with Lit's live directive. Also write user
changes back to the item, or they are lost when the item leaves the window.
To get new DOM for each item, wrap the content in Lit's keyed directive
with the item key:  html${keyed(ctx.value.id, content)} .
- **keyFunction**: `VirtualScrollKeyFunction<T> | null` — A function that returns a unique key for an item. Receives the item and its index in data.

An item keeps its rendered element while its key stays in the rendered window. The elements
of keys that leave the window are reused for keys that enter it. Without it, the index is the
key, so after a data change an index keeps its element and shows its new item. Set it when
items move within data, for example on sort, insert or remove.
- **orientation**: `"vertical" | "horizontal"` — The scroll axis of the component.
- **overScan**: `number` — Number of extra items to render beyond the visible area of the viewport.
Higher values reduce blank flashes during fast scrolling but can lower performance.
- **layoutComplete**: `any` — Resolves when the virtual scroll has settled: the current render pass is
complete, the item-size measurements it triggers are complete, and so
are the renders those measurements schedule.

`updateComplete` covers one Lit render pass. This covers `data` changes,
scrolls, and viewport resizes, where the stable DOM state comes after
one or more follow-up renders.
- **scrollToIndex**(index: number, options?: ScrollIntoViewOptions): Promise<void> — Scrolls to the specified item index.

block (inline in the horizontal orientation) positions the item as in
scrollIntoView, and defaults to start. With nearest, the item
scrolls the smallest distance that brings it into view.

Items outside the rendered window have only an estimated size, so the
first jump can miss the target. The items at the landing point are then
measured, and the scroll position is corrected. This repeats until the
offset is stable.

A hidden or detached list cannot scroll. It keeps the call and scrolls
when it shows. A newer call replaces the kept one.

The returned promise resolves when the scroll settles on the final,
corrected offset, or when a newer call replaces this one. Callers that
need only the first, approximate scroll can ignore it.

## Interfaces

### [BaseColumnConfiguration](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/BaseColumnConfiguration)
Configuration object for grid columns.

- **cellTemplate?**: `any` — Cell template callback.
- **dataType?**: `DataType` — The type of data this column will reference.

Affects the default filter operands if the column is with filtering enabled.
- **field**: `K` — The field from the data for this column.
- **filterable?**: `boolean` — Whether the column can be filtered.
- **filteringCaseSensitive?**: `boolean` — Whether the filter operations will be case sensitive.
- **header?**: `string` — Optional text to display in the column header. By default, the column field is used
to render the header text.
- **headerTemplate?**: `any` — Header template callback.
- **hidden?**: `boolean` — Whether the column is hidden or not.
- **resizable?**: `boolean` — Whether the column can be resized or not.
- **sortable?**: `boolean` — Whether the column can be sorted.
- **sortConfiguration?**: `ColumnSortConfiguration<T, K>` — Sort configuration options for the column (e.g., custom comparer).
- **sortingCaseSensitive?**: `boolean` — Whether the sort operations will be case sensitive.
- **width?**: `string` — Width for the current column.

Accepts most CSS units for controlling width.

### [BaseColumnSortConfiguration](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/BaseColumnSortConfiguration)
Extended sort configuration for a column.

- **comparer?**: `SortComparer<T, K>` — Custom comparer function for sort operations for this column.

### [BaseFilterExpression](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/BaseFilterExpression)
Represents a filter operation for a given column.

- **caseSensitive?**: `boolean` — Whether the filter operation should be case sensitive.
- **condition**: `FilterOperation<PropertyType<T, K>> | OperandKeys<PropertyType<T, K>>` — The filter function which will be executed against the data records.
- **criteria?**: `FilterCriteria` — Dictates how this expression should resolve in the filter operation in relation to
other expressions.
- **key**: `K` — The target column for the filter operation.
- **searchTerm?**: `PropertyType<T, K>` — The filtering value used in the filter condition function.

### [BaseIgcCellContext](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/BaseIgcCellContext)
Context object for the row cell template callback.

- **column**: `ColumnConfiguration<T, K>` — The current configuration for the column.
- **parent**: `IgcGridLiteCell<T>` — The cell element parent of the template.
- **row**: `IgcGridLiteRow<T>` — The row element containing the cell.
- **value**: `PropertyType<T, K>` — The value from the data source for this cell.

### [BaseSortingExpression](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/BaseSortingExpression)
Represents a sort operation for a given column.

- **caseSensitive?**: `boolean` — Whether the sort operation should be case sensitive.
- **comparer?**: `SortComparer<T, K>` — Custom comparer function for this operation.
- **direction**: `SortingDirection` — Sort direction for this operation.
- **key**: `K` — The target column.

### [ChatAttachmentRenderContext](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/ChatAttachmentRenderContext)
Extends: ChatMessageRenderContext
The context object for renderers that deal with a specific attachment within a message.
It extends the message context with the attachment data.

- **attachment**: `IgcChatMessageAttachment` — The specific attachment being rendered.

### [ChatInputRenderContext](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/ChatInputRenderContext)

The context object for renderers that deal with the chat input area.
It extends the base context with input-specific properties.

- **attachments**: `IgcChatMessageAttachment[]` — The list of attachments currently in the input area.

valueKey and displayKey fields are set, and each contains the group value.

### [DatePartDeltas](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/DatePartDeltas)
The amounts by which each date or time part is incremented or decremented on
a step action in date-time input; every part defaults to 1.

- **date?**: `number` — The number of days the date part is spun by.
- **hours?**: `number` — The number of hours the hours part is spun by.
- **minutes?**: `number` — The number of minutes the minutes part is spun by.
- **month?**: `number` — The number of months the month part is spun by.
- **seconds?**: `number` — The number of seconds the seconds part is spun by.
- **year?**: `number` — The number of years the year part is spun by.

### [DateRangeDescriptor](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/DateRangeDescriptor)
Describes a set of dates by combining a range type with the dates it applies to.

- **dateRange?**: `Date[]` — The date or dates the descriptor applies to, interpreted according to DateRangeDescriptor.type.
DateRangeType.After and DateRangeType.Before use the first date,
DateRangeType.Between uses the first and the last, and
DateRangeType.Specific matches every date listed. Not used by
DateRangeType.Weekdays and DateRangeType.Weekends.
- **label?**: `string` — What the dates mean, for example 'Free delivery'. The calendar adds the label
to the accessible name of each matching date, so assistive technologies announce it.
- **type**: `DateRangeType` — The kind of range being described, which determines how DateRangeDescriptor.dateRange is matched.

### [FilteringOptions](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/FilteringOptions)
Filtering options for the combo component.

- **caseSensitive?**: `boolean` — Determines whether the filtering operation should be case sensitive.
- **filterKey**: `any | undefined` — The key in the data source used when filtering the list of options.
- **matchDiacritics?**: `boolean` — When true, the filter distinguishes between accented letters and their base letters.
- **mode?**: `ComboFilteringMode` — Where the filtering runs. With remote, the combo does not filter the
options: the application sets data on igcSearchInput, and appends to
it on igcDataRequest. Default is local.

### [FilterOperation](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/FilterOperation)

- **type?**: `string` — The MIME type or a custom type identifier for the attachment (e.g. "image/png", "pdf", "audio").
- **url?**: `string` — The URL from which the attachment can be downloaded or viewed.
Typically used for attachments stored on a server or CDN.
