### [IgrChatOptions](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/IgrChatOptions)
Configuration options for customizing the behavior and appearance of the chat component.

- **acceptedFiles?**: `string` — The accepted files that could be attached.
Defines the file types as a list of comma-separated values (e.g. "image/*,.pdf") that the file input should accept.
- **adoptRootStyles?**: `boolean` — A boolean flag that, when true, enables a **quick and dirty workaround** for styling
components rendered within the Shadow DOM, from custom message renderers, by allowing them
to inherit styles from the document's root. This can be useful for developers who prefer not to handle
Shadow DOM encapsulation, but it is **not the recommended approach**.

It is highly advised to use standard Web Component styling methods first, in this order:

1.  **CSS Variables and Parts API**: Use the exposed ::part API with custom CSS variables to style
your content in your custom renderers.

2.  **link elements**: For larger style sheets, link them directly within the Shadow DOM to maintain
encapsulation.

3.  **Inline <style> tags**: Use these for small, self-contained styles within a template.

This property should be used as a **last resort** as it can lead to **style leakage**, where
global styles unexpectedly bleed into the component, breaking encapsulation and causing
unpredictable visual issues.
- **currentUserId?**: `string` — The ID of the current user. Used to differentiate between incoming and outgoing messages.
- **disableAutoScroll?**: `boolean` — If true, prevents the chat from automatically scrolling to the latest message.
- **disableInputAttachments?**: `boolean` — If true, disables the ability to upload and send attachments.
Defaults to false.
- **headerText?**: `string` — Optional header text to display at the top of the chat component.
- **inputPlaceholder?**: `string` — Optional placeholder text for the chat input area.
Provides a hint to the user about what they can type (e.g. "Type a message...").
- **isTyping?**: `boolean` — Indicates whether the other user is currently typing a message.
- **renderers?**: `ChatRenderers` — An object containing a collection of custom renderers for different parts of the chat UI.
- **stopTypingDelay?**: `number` — Time in milliseconds to wait before dispatching a stop typing event.
Default is 3000.
- **suggestions?**: `string[]` — Suggested text snippets or quick replies that can be shown as user-selectable options.
- **suggestionsPosition?**: `ChatSuggestionsPosition` — Controls the position of the chat suggestions within the component layout.

- "below-input": Renders suggestions below the chat input area.
- "below-messages": Renders suggestions below the chat messages area.

Default is "below-messages".

- **startDate?**: `string`
- **weekLabel?**: `string`
- **yearToDate?**: `string`

### [IgrFilteredEvent](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/IgrFilteredEvent)
Event object for the filtered event of the grid.

- **key**: `Keys<T>` — The target column for the filter operation.
- **state**: `FilterExpression<T>[]` — The filter state of the column after the operation.

### [IgrFilteringEvent](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/IgrFilteringEvent)
Event object for the filtering event of the grid.

- **expressions**: `FilterExpression<T>[]` — The filter expression(s) to apply.
- **key**: `Keys<T>` — The target column for the filter operation.
- **type**: `"remove" | "add" | "modify"` — The type of modification which will be applied to the filter
state of the column.

### [IgrHeaderContext](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/IgrHeaderContext)
Context object for the column header template callback.

- **column**: `ColumnConfiguration<T, any> | ColumnConfiguration<T, Exclude<any & string, any>> | ColumnConfiguration<T, Exclude<any, any>>` — The current configuration for the column.
- **parent**: `IgcGridLiteHeader<T>` — The header element parent of the template.

### [IgrRadioChangeEventArgsDetail](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/IgrRadioChangeEventArgsDetail)

- **checked**: `boolean`
- **value?**: `string`

### [IgrRangeSliderValueEventArgsDetail](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/IgrRangeSliderValueEventArgsDetail)

- **lower**: `number`
- **upper**: `number`

### [IgrSplitterLayoutChangedEventArgsDetail](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/IgrSplitterLayoutChangedEventArgsDetail)

- **endCollapsed**: `boolean` — Whether the end pane is currently collapsed
- **endSize**: `string` — The current size of the end pane
- **startCollapsed**: `boolean` — Whether the start pane is currently collapsed
- **startSize**: `string` — The current size of the start pane

### [IgrSplitterResizeEventArgsDetail](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/IgrSplitterResizeEventArgsDetail)

- **delta?**: `number` — The change in size since the resize operation started (only for igcResizing and igcResizeEnd)
- **endPanelSize**: `number` — The current size of the end panel in pixels
- **startPanelSize**: `number` — The current size of the start panel in pixels

### [IgrTileChangeStateEventArgsDetail](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/IgrTileChangeStateEventArgsDetail)

- **state**: `boolean`
- **tile**: `IgcTileComponent`

### [IgrTreeSelectionEventArgsDetail](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/IgrTreeSelectionEventArgsDetail)

- **newSelection**: `IgcTreeItemComponent[]`

### [ISplitterResourceStrings](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/ISplitterResourceStrings)

- **splitter_resize_panes?**: `string`

### [ITileResourceStrings](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/ITileResourceStrings)

- **tile_enter_fullscreen?**: `string`
- **tile_exit_fullscreen?**: `string`
- **tile_maximize?**: `string`
- **tile_restore?**: `string`

### [ITooltipResourceStrings](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/ITooltipResourceStrings)

- **tooltip_close?**: `string`

### [ITreeResourceStrings](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/ITreeResourceStrings)

- **collapse?**: `string`
- **expand?**: `string`

### [NavigateToOptions](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/NavigateToOptions)
Options for the navigateTo API of the grid.

- **activate?**: `boolean` — When true, the navigated cell becomes the active cell.
- **column?**: `Keys<T>` — The column field to navigate to. Without it, only the row scrolls into view.

### [QrCodeCopyOptions](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/QrCodeCopyOptions)
Options for copying the QR code to the clipboard.

- **format?**: `QrCodeCopyFormat` — The image format. An svg copy also holds a PNG image for applications that do not read SVG.
- **scale?**: `number` — Multiplier applied to the size of the component. A 256px QR code with a scale of 2 copies as a 512x512 image.

### [QrCodeExportOptions](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/QrCodeExportOptions)
Options for exporting the QR code to a file.

- **download?**: `boolean` — Whether to open the browser download dialog for the exported file.
- **fileName?**: `string` — The name of the exported file. The extension of the format is appended when the name does not end with it.
- **format?**: `QrCodeExportFormat` — The output format.
- **scale?**: `number` — Multiplier applied to the size of the component. A 256px QR code with a scale of 2 exports as a 512x512 image.
For svg, the multiplier applies to the width and height attributes while the viewBox is unchanged.

### [RegisterIconOptions](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/RegisterIconOptions)
Options for registering an SVG icon.

- **collection?**: `string` — The collection to register the icon in.
- **stripMeta?**: `boolean` — Whether to strip SVG meta elements (<title> and <desc>) from the icon
before storing it.

### [VirtualScrollDataRequest](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/VirtualScrollDataRequest)
A request for more data, emitted when the rendered window comes near the
end of the loaded items. Consumers listen for it and append the requested
items.

- **count**: `number` — Number of items being requested.
- **startIndex**: `number` — The first index that does not yet have data.
Append at least count more items starting here.

### [VirtualScrollItemContext](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/VirtualScrollItemContext)
Context passed to the item template: the item data, its index, and utility
properties for rendering.

- **count**: `number` — The total number of items
- **index**: `number` — The index of the current item
- **value**: `T` — The current item in the virtual scroll
- **isFirst**: `any`
- **isLast**: `any`

### [VirtualScrollState](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/interfaces/VirtualScrollState)
Snapshot of the currently rendered virtual window

- **endIndex**: `number` — The index of the last item currently rendered in the viewport (inclusive).
- **startIndex**: `number` — The index of the first item currently rendered in the viewport.
- **totalSize**: `number` — The total size of the virtual scroll content in pixels.
- **viewportSize**: `number` — The size of the viewport in pixels.

## Enumerations

### [DatePart](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/enums/DatePart)
Date/time part classes of the date-time input. Each date part type has its own class;
the time parts share one class. Only the types and the factory are exported.

- **AmPm** = "amPm"
- **Date** = "date"
- **Hours** = "hours"
- **Minutes** = "minutes"
- **Month** = "month"
- **Seconds** = "seconds"
- **Year** = "year"

### [DateRangeType](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/enums/DateRangeType)

- **After** = 0
- **Before** = 1
- **Between** = 2
- **Specific** = 3
- **Weekdays** = 4
- **Weekends** = 5

## Functions

### [configureTheme](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/functions/configureTheme)
`configureTheme(t: "material" | "bootstrap" | "indigo" | "fluent", v?: "light" | "dark"): void`
Allows the global configuration of the active theme.

Usage:
  import { configureTheme } from 'igniteui-webcomponents';

 configureTheme('material', 'light');

### [setCurrentI18n](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/functions/setCurrentI18n)
`setCurrentI18n(locale: string): void`
Set the current locale of all Ignite UI components.

### [setIconRef](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/functions/setIconRef)
`setIconRef(name: string, collection: string, icon: IconMeta): void`
Sets an icon reference/alias that points to another icon.

### [θaddAdoptedStylesController](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/functions/θaddAdoptedStylesController)
`θaddAdoptedStylesController(host: ReactiveControllerHost & LitElement): AdoptedStylesController`
Creates an AdoptedStylesController and adds it to a Lit component.

### [θaddThemingController](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/functions/θaddThemingController)
`θaddThemingController(host: ReactiveControllerHost & ReactiveElement, themes: ComponentThemes, config?: ThemingControllerConfig): ThemingController`
Creates and attaches a ThemingController to the given host element.

This is the preferred way to add theming support to a component. The controller
is registered with the host's reactive controller lifecycle and automatically
resolves the active theme from an ancestor theme provider context or
falls back to the application-wide theme set via configureTheme().

### [θcreateAbortHandle](https://www.infragistics.com/api/react/igniteui-react/19.11/functions/θcreateAbortHandle)
`θcreateAbortHandle(): AbortHandle`
Creates an AbortHandle, which wraps an AbortController and gives a
signal that the caller can reset. An abort or a reset installs a new
controller, so the caller keeps the same handle.
